headline: Chicago November scrap trades up $30 on shred, $20 on busheling
detail: A Chicago source says shredded and heavy grades like plate and structural and rail wheels rose about $30 a gross ton, with busheling up $20, as integrated mills chase scarce heavy scrap. Nationally mills paid $20 more for primes and $30 more for obsolete grades as the month nears its settle.

headline: Copper bounces Monday as China runs short of refined metal
detail: COMEX and LME copper edged higher Monday after Shanghai warehouse stocks fell about 24% last week to their lowest since January 2024 and China's import premium hit a record. Traders now wait on US inflation data, since a hot reading would lift the dollar and weigh on copper scrap bids.

headline: TD warns copper could slide another $500 after hitting its lowest since July
detail: LME copper ended Friday near $13,780 a ton as the Democratic midterm gains cut the odds of a US refined copper tariff and raised doubts about data-center demand. With about 1.6 million tons stockpiled in the US, dropping the tariff could shrink the COMEX premium that has propped up US scrap values.

headline: Strong October jobs report lifts odds of a December Fed rate hike
detail: Employers added 165,000 jobs against about 60,000 expected, and unemployment fell to 4.1%, pushing December hike odds to around 77-80% and the 10-year yield to 4.87%. Higher rates and a firmer dollar weigh on gold and copper.

headline: BC unions refuse to handle copper from the striking Highland Valley mine
detail: The BC Federation of Labour told affiliated unions not to handle, ship or process copper and molybdenum concentrate from Teck's Highland Valley mine, where about 1,200 workers have been on strike since Oct 24. The mine is running at reduced capacity, and a shipping boycott would further tighten copper concentrate supply.

headline: Gold rebounds above $4,100 ahead of Tuesday's inflation report
detail: Spot gold rose about 1% early Monday to roughly $4,110 as oil fell and the dollar eased, after posting its best week since August. A hot CPI reading on Tuesday could revive the dollar and cap the rally.

headline: Platinum jumps 8% and palladium 5% over the week
detail: Platinum closed Friday near $1,538 an ounce and palladium near $1,023, riding a broad rally in precious metals. That gives a lift to catalytic converter values after a long slide, though both metals remain below their longer-term averages.

headline: Lutnick restarts Canada trade talks focused on steel, aluminum and autos
detail: Commerce is pushing to revive talks centered on the Section 232 tariffs of up to 50% on steel, aluminum and copper, with a possible steel quota and aluminum cut discussed earlier. Any deal would loosen cross-border metal flows and could narrow the US Midwest aluminum premium.

headline: Nucor lifts its coil price for a 15th straight week to $1,280
detail: Nucor raised its weekly hot-rolled coil spot price by $10 to $1,280 a short ton, with tariffs keeping US sheet prices near four-year highs. Strong coil prices keep mills buying prime scrap aggressively.

headline: Nickel holds near its highs even after a strong US jobs report
detail: Shanghai nickel stayed firm Monday after last week's rally on talk of Indonesian supply limits, even though October payrolls of 165,000 lifted the odds of a December Fed hike to about 78%. Firm nickel supports stainless and alloy scrap prices.

headline: Silver rose 5.5% last week while copper fell 3.7%
detail: Silver closed the week near $51.80 and gold gained 4.5%, but Comex copper fell to about $6.22/lb, below support near $6.30. Softer copper is a headwind for No. 1 and No. 2 copper scrap bids.

headline: China factory-gate prices rise 5.7%, fastest since 2022
detail: October producer prices beat forecasts on higher energy and electronics costs, while consumer inflation slowed to 0.7%. Rising factory prices support global metal prices, but weak consumer demand shows the economy is still uneven.

headline: Dollar jumps on hike bets as oil drops on Iran hopes
detail: The dollar index rose 0.74% Friday to about 102.3, while Brent fell near $97 on hopes the Iran conflict may end. Cheaper oil eases inflation fears, but a stronger dollar makes metals more expensive for overseas buyers.

headline: Sibanye cuts its Montana palladium output forecast after a strike
detail: Sibanye-Stillwater lowered its 2026 US mine guidance to 245,000-255,000 ounces from 280,000-300,000 after a five-week strike. Less newly mined palladium makes recycled converter metal more important and supports its value.

headline: Codelco admits it overstated copper output by 42,100 tons
detail: Chile's state miner found that unfinished material had been booked as finished copper to hit targets, and it fired nine employees. Codelco's real output has fallen to about 1.2 million tons a year, a reminder that mine supply is tighter than reported.

headline: October US new-vehicle sales pace slows to about 15.5 million
detail: Cox Automotive estimates the October selling pace at 15.5 million, the slowest since January, with retail weak and fleet sales up; Ford's EV sales fell about 71%. Softer retail demand could trim auto output and the flow of prompt industrial scrap.

headline: Fastmarkets survey pointed to about 7% higher US scrap for November
detail: The monthly trend survey implied roughly a 7% rise, citing strong mill order books, higher coil prices and thin flows into yards, with dealer inventories reading tighter. Trading so far has lined up with that call.

headline: US construction spending fell 1.9% in September, led by housing
detail: Census data released Nov 2 showed total spending at a $2.19 trillion annual rate, with private residential down 5.5% while data-center spending kept climbing. Weak homebuilding cuts demand for rebar, wire and copper plumbing, but data centers are a bright spot for copper and aluminum.

headline: China's October trade figures due Tuesday; exports seen staying strong
detail: A Reuters poll expects export growth stayed strong in October after September's surge. Import figures for copper, iron ore and aluminum will signal China's appetite for metals and scrap.

headline: Aluminum stocks keep falling but Chinese demand is soft
detail: LME aluminum stocks fell about 5% over the month to roughly 227,000 tons and Shanghai warrants dropped by more than half, yet China's aluminum processing index slipped below 50 in October. SMM expects prices to move sideways, which keeps aluminum scrap steady rather than rising.

headline: Democrats set to take Congress after midterms fought over tariffs
detail: Democrats are expected to control both chambers in January after voters said tariffs hurt the economy, raising pressure to roll some duties back. The Section 232 metals tariffs are not likely to change quickly, but a policy shift could matter for 2027 metal premiums.

headline: Iron ore slips as Chinese mills buy only what they need
detail: Dalian iron ore futures fell about 1.8% on Nov 5 as thin margins kept Chinese steelmakers from restocking, and Vale's chief said China's steel output has probably peaked above 1 billion tons a year. Weak Chinese steel demand caps global ferrous prices and can push cheap Chinese steel exports.

headline: Tesla to end Cybertruck production in Texas by mid-2027
detail: Musk said the Austin plant will wind down the stainless-steel Cybertruck to make room for the Cybercab robotaxi. It is another sign of shrinking US EV truck output.
